author: Sam Stark
title: Austin unveils new baggage system, part of $3.8B airport expansion project - NewsBreak
text:
By Sam Stark ,
6 hours ago
AUSTIN (KXAN) — City leaders on Tuesday celebrated an early milestone in the massive Austin Bergstrom International Airport project.
The city is in the midst of its largest-ever airport expansion. It will cost around $3.8 billion and have the capacity to welcome 37 million travelers annually – nearly double the airport’s current capacity. Officials expect the expansion to wrap up by 2030.
“Good things are happening in Austin, Texas, and our airport has to move with it,” said Austin Mayor Kirk Watson at a Wednesday morning press event. “Importantly, though, for an airport to move, baggage needs to move.”
City leaders on Tuesday premiered the new Outbound Baggage Handling System, designed to move luggage faster, reduce flight delays and support the region’s growth. The upgrade can process double the number of bags – around 4,000 an hour – as the previous system.
“The new outbound baggage handling system is a critical investment in the passenger experience,” Watson said. “The estimated $241 million investment is part of our larger vision to ensure that the AUS remains a world-class travel hub that is fully equipped so that it can handle today’s needs and will be in a position to handle tomorrow’s opportunities.”
Once the expansion is complete , AUS will have a new concourse with more than 20 gates, additional parking structures and a new arrival and departure hall.
Mayor Pro Tem Vanessa Fuentes said the baggage project reflects the city’s broader vision for responsible, sustainable growth. “This project is more than just about moving luggage. It’s about moving our city,” she said.
The baggage system was finished several months ahead of schedule, some positive news after the aviation department recently faced scrutiny. A city audit released earlier this month found the department had failed to properly manage hundreds of vendor contracts.
Watson mentioned the audit in his latest “Watson Wire” newsletter released on Wednesday morning.
“At the airport, we were falling behind where we needed to be. An outside consultant reviewed operations and helped create benchmarking with other large airports on dealing with a multi-billion-dollar program. Changes were made. That place is now humming ,” he wrote.
